label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic and one fault from klaxon.faults injected on purpose (synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money). It records what the fault looks like from the outside; it is not the Klaxon agent.

fault.name: pool-exhaustion
fault.title: Payments fail: the payments API's database pool runs dry
fault.cause: a deploy of the payments API with a connection leak (REFUND_CONNECTION=kept): reading a payment's refunds takes a connection from its database pool of 10 and never gives it back, so after about ten refunds the pool is empty, and every request waits 5 s for a connection, then fails with a 500
expected_symptoms: POST /payments takes about 5 s and fails with a 500: the 5xx share and the p95 latency climb
the payments API logs 'unhandled error' with PoolTimeout: no connection within 5 s
its health check fails: it cannot get a connection either, while PostgreSQL itself is up
the money check passes: a payment that never got a connection was never charged
fault.remedy: roll the payments API back to REFUND_CONNECTION=returned: its new container starts with a full pool

provider_behavior: the provider's behavior was put back as it was found
printed_output: Klaxon week 2: a fault injected on purpose: pool-exhaustion
